title: perf(canary): automated detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Adds an automated regression detector for the performance canary pipeline (latency and throughput), integrates hysteresis thresholds, and wires rollout guard actions to the rollout controller. Motivation: we observed repeated manual interventions when canaries flapped during noisy windows. This change implements an automated detector that ingests canary metrics, applies adaptive baselines + hysteresis, and triggers rollout guards (pause/rollback/notify) when violations are sustained.

What changed (high-level): - New detector service: services/perf-canary/detector (in-process library + service adapter) - Hysteresis & threshold logic configurable per-metric and per-model - Rollout guard integration: calls into services/rollout/controller API to pause or rollback a rollout - Metric extraction updates: small changes to exporters to emit per-route p95/p99, mean latency, and throughput counters with stable tagging - Dashboards and alerting: Grafana dashboard + alert rules for manual monitoring - Tests: unit tests for detector logic, integration test for canary->rollout flow - Feature flagging + rollout: gated behind FF perf_canary_autodetect (default off)

Checklist:
- [x] Detector algorithm implemented with configurable hysteresis windows
- [x] Safe defaults and canary-specific overrides added
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Docs & runbook updated
- [x] Feature-flagged and smoke-tested in staging

Testing performed: Local unit test suite + CI, staging end-to-end run with synthetic traffic (2k requests/min) for two canary variants for 24 hours. Observed correct detection of injected 15% latency regression and subsequent pause of rollout.

Rollout notes: Feature is behind feature flag perf_canary_autodetect. When enabled the detector will automatically request the rollout controller to PAUSE a rollout on sustained regressions (>3 consecutive windows by default) and can request AUTOMATED_ROLLBACK if configured. Operators can override or force-continue via the rollout console.

Backward compatibility: All changes are opt-in via feature flag. Exporter metric names are additive; existing dashboards/alerts remain functional.

Related tickets: ENG-4521 (canary detector), ENG-4708 (rollout guard integration), SUP-9823 (customer incident that motivated hysteresis tuning).

review_comments: Marco Li: Please add a conservative default for the hysteresis window; we should avoid sensitivity to short spikes. (resolved: default set to 3 windows)
Priya Desai: Ensure we fail-safe if rollout controller is unreachable — detector should not block rollouts when controller is down. (resolved: detector will log and emit alert but not block)
Evan Thompson: Can the detector expose a dry-run mode so we can observe what it would have done historically? (added: dry_run=true config and a one-shot historical replayer)
Asha Kapoor (author): Addressed comments, added unit tests around hysteresis and unreachable rollout controller behavior, added dry-run replayer script. Marking for final review.

merge_summary: Squash-merged to main. Triggered staging deploy of feature flag perf_canary_autodetect=false (flag off by default). Manual enable required to activate in prod. No hotfix required.
release_notes: Add automated performance regression detection for canaries (latency & throughput).
Introduce hysteresis thresholds and safe defaults to reduce noisy flaps.
Integrate detector with rollout controller to pause/rollback canaries on sustained regressions.
New Grafana dashboard and operator runbook included.
notes_for_ops: Feature is gated by perf_canary_autodetect. Config live keys: perf_canary.hysteresis.windows=3, perf_canary.alert_window=60s. To enable: flip flag in feature-flag service then monitor dashboards 'Perf Canary / Detector'. Run the historical dry-run replayer (scripts/perf_canary/replay) to validate against past traffic before enabling in prod.
risk_assessment: Low-Medium: algorithm is opt-in and fail-safe if rollout controller unreachable. Main risk is noisy detector sensitivity — mitigated by conservative defaults and dry-run validation.
